citeAs: Pratap, V., Xu, Q., Sriram, A., Synnaeve, G., Collobert, R. (2020). MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411.
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert (Facebook AI Research)
description: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) is a large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research, derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. It consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Polish). The dataset also includes Language Models (LM) and baseline Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models for all languages.
inLanguage: en, de, nl, fr, es, it, pt, pl
name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: WER between generated transcript (GT) and human rated transcript (HRT) was measured for dev and test sets across all 8 languages. WER ranged from 1.93% (Spanish dev) to 12.64% (Portuguese dev). For English: dev 4.55%, test 4.54%; German: dev 3.6%, test 3.9%; Dutch: dev 7.24%, test 8.61%; French: dev 3.33%, test 4.45%; Spanish: dev 1.93%, test 3.07%; Italian: dev 6.8%, test 5.37%; Portuguese: dev 12.64%, test 12.07%; Polish: dev 5.67%, test 5.12%.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom human verification workflow (human transcribers listened to audio and corrected transcripts for dev and test sets)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts were generated via a pipeline: (1) pseudo labels generated using beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model on acoustic models; (2) transcript retrieval by matching pseudo labels to source book text using TF-IDF similarity on bigrams and Smith-Waterman alignment; (3) candidate transcripts with WER > 40% between candidate and pseudo label were filtered out. For development and test sets, human transcribers listened to audio while viewing the transcript and corrected clear and obvious errors only.
rai:dataBiases: English is heavily dominant in LibriVox data (71,506 hours vs. a few hundred to a few thousand hours for other languages). The dataset is derived from audiobooks (read speech), which may not represent natural conversational speech. To avoid introducing bias from human transcription, transcribers were instructed to only correct "clear and obvious" errors. Gender balance was explicitly enforced in dev and test sets. The MLS English dev/test sets were designed to be harder than LibriSpeech dev-/test-other partitions by selecting speakers with higher WER.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by downloading audiobooks from LibriVox in 8 languages (English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish) using data preparation tools from the LibriLight open source library. Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Text sources for the audiobooks were downloaded from multiple domains including gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, and hathitrust.org for English, and via manual approaches (browser copy, PDF/EPUB extraction, HTML parsers) for other languages.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of audiobooks from LibriVox (read speech) and corresponding book texts from Project Gutenberg and other online sources. LibriVox provided over 71,500 hours of English audio and thousands of hours in other languages. Audio files ranged from a few minutes to hours in duration at 48kHz.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks (read speech), which may not generalize to conversational or spontaneous speech. Language coverage is limited to 8 languages. For Polish, the OOV rate is 13.39% which negatively impacts LM-based decoding. Some audiobook text sources were unavailable or had invalid links, limiting coverage. The pseudo-label-based transcript retrieval may introduce transcription errors, particularly for numbers and rare words with hyphens/apostrophes.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Dataset was split into train, development, and test sets with no speaker overlap across splits. Speakers were balanced by gender and duration in dev and test sets. Speakers with duration shorter than a threshold were assigned to training; remaining speakers were split equally by gender into dev and test. Speakers with high duration were truncated by sampling recordings up to an upper bound. Limited supervision subsets were created: 10-hour, 1-hour, and six 10-minute sets, with balanced male/female speaker sampling.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio files were downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Audio was segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models (TDS Convolutions with ASG loss) to find silence intervals. Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of punctuations/subscripts/superscripts/emojis/escape symbols, removal of end-of-line hyphens, filtering of characters outside valid unicode ranges per language orthography. Numbers in transcripts were replaced with aligned words from pseudo labels. Heuristics were applied for handling hyphens and apostrophes.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to open new avenues in ASR and TTS research by providing a large, freely available multilingual speech corpus. It promotes open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and multilingual ASR, potentially benefiting speakers of multiple languages beyond English.
rai:dataUseCases: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research, Text-To-Speech (TTS) research, multilingual ASR, large-scale training of ASR systems, low-resource speech recognition benchmarking.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Acoustic models using Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss were used for audio segmentation and pseudo-label generation. A pre-trained model using TDS encoder and CTC loss (trained on LibriSpeech and LibriVox pseudo labels) was used for English. A 4-gram language model was used for beam-search decoding to generate pseudo labels. TF-IDF similarity on bigrams was used for document retrieval. Smith-Waterman alignment was used for transcript matching. An SVM gender classifier with RBF kernel (trained on LibriSpeech speakers) was used to label speaker gender. The wav2letter@anywhere framework was used for streaming inference.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Training data for acoustic models used in segmentation was derived from videos publicly shared by users; this data was completely de-identified. The MLS dataset itself is derived from public domain audiobooks and does not contain personal or sensitive information.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify a fixed number of independent annotations per item; human verification was done once per item for dev/test sets.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No demographic information about human transcribers/annotators is provided in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: While the paper mentions some audiobook text sources were unavailable or had invalid links, it does not describe a systematic missing data handling protocol beyond manual searching for alternatives.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol for missing values is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
